_comment: Hand-authored. The generated clusters start at knowledge-time 1830, which leaves the 1650-1830 stretch of the knowledge rail empty. These are the claims that made deep time thinkable at all, plus the superseded ages of the Earth. Scrubbing knowledge-time to 1880 should collapse the planet to ~100 Myr old: that is the whole thesis in one drag. Every citation here is a canonical work chosen because its existence is not in doubt.

claims.statement: Rock layers were laid down in sequence, the lowest first, so strata record an order of events.
claims.asserted_by: Steno 1669, De solido intra solidum naturaliter contento prodromus

status_timeline.source: Steno 1669, Florence — superposition, original horizontality and lateral continuity, from dissecting Tuscan hillsides
stratigraphic practice, c. 1800 — superposition becomes the working assumption of field geology

claims.statement: The rock cycle has run so long that the record shows no vestige of a beginning and no prospect of an end.
claims.asserted_by: Hutton 1788, Transactions of the Royal Society of Edinburgh

status_timeline.source: Hutton 1788 — the angular unconformity at Siccar Point read as two complete cycles of deposition, uplift and erosion
scriptural geology, c. 1800 — an indefinitely old Earth is resisted on theological grounds
geological consensus, c. 1840 — an Earth vastly older than human record is taken as established

claims.statement: Present-day rates of erosion and deposition are enough to explain the past; no former catastrophes need be invoked.

status_timeline.source: Lyell 1830-1833 — Hutton's deep time restated as strict uniformity of rate as well as of process
geological consensus, c. 1860 — uniformitarianism becomes the disciplinary default
Alvarez et al. 1980, Science — a sudden extraterrestrial catastrophe reopens the question of rate

claims.statement: The Earth's heat loss limits its age to somewhere between twenty and four hundred million years, most likely about a hundred.
claims.asserted_by: Thomson (Kelvin) 1862, Transactions of the Royal Society of Edinburgh

status_timeline.source: Thomson 1862, On the Secular Cooling of the Earth — a cooling sphere with no internal heat source
physical consensus, 1870s-1890s — Kelvin's authority compresses the geological timescale against the objections of geologists and of Darwin
Curie & Laborde 1903, Comptes Rendus — radium generates heat, so the Earth is not a simply cooling body
Holmes 1913, The Age of the Earth — radiometric ages exceed Kelvin's ceiling outright

claims.statement: Lead accumulating in uranium minerals gives rock ages from four hundred million up to two thousand million years.

status_timeline.source: Boltwood 1907 — the first uranium-lead ages, on ten mineral samples
age-of-the-Earth debate, 1920s — radiometric ages accepted in principle, the numbers still moving
Patterson 1956 — the meteoritic lead isochron settles the figure near 4.55 Ga

claims.statement: Radioactive decay makes the Earth at least sixteen hundred million years old, far beyond any cooling estimate.
claims.asserted_by: Holmes 1913, The Age of the Earth (Harper & Brothers)

status_timeline.source: Holmes 1913 — the first sustained argument for a radiometric geological timescale
National Research Council report on the age of the Earth, 1931 — radiometric dating formally endorsed
Patterson 1956 — superseded by the meteoritic lead isochron

claims.statement: Matching Carboniferous floras and glacial beds on now-separate continents mean the landmasses were once joined.
claims.asserted_by: Wegener 1915, Die Entstehung der Kontinente und Ozeane

status_timeline.source: Wegener 1915 — Pangaea argued from the fit of coastlines and the distribution of the Glossopteris flora
American Association of Petroleum Geologists symposium, 1926-1928 — drift rejected, largely for lacking a mechanism
Vine & Matthews 1963, Nature — magnetic striping on the seafloor supplies the missing mechanism
Morgan 1968 and Le Pichon 1968 — plate tectonics becomes the framework of the earth sciences

claims.statement: The Cretaceous-Tertiary boundary sits at sixty-five million years, the round figure carried by textbooks for decades.
claims.asserted_by: Cretaceous-Tertiary boundary age, textbook consensus c. 1980-2005 (no single originating paper)

status_timeline.source: timescale consensus, 1980s-1990s — deliberately vague attribution; 65 Ma was a rounded figure in general circulation, not one group's result
Renne et al. 2013, Science — recalibration moves the boundary to 66.043 Ma and the round number retires

claims.statement: Argon dating of boundary tektites and ash puts the extinction at 66.043 million years, to within eleven thousand.

status_timeline.source: Renne et al. 2013, Science — Time Scales of Critical Events Around the Cretaceous-Paleogene Boundary
geochronological consensus, mid-2010s — 66.0 Ma adopted by the international timescale

claims.statement: The second great freeze, the Marinoan, ends at 635 million years, the boundary that now opens the Ediacaran.

status_timeline.source: Condon et al. 2005, Science — U-Pb ages from the Doushantuo Formation, South China
chronostratigraphic consensus — 635 Ma ratified as the base of the Ediacaran, at the top of the Marinoan cap carbonate

edges.label: coal forests sit inside Earth history
edges.asserted_by: Steno 1669, De solido intra solidum naturaliter contento prodromus
